page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The server is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 262 GB drive, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between compute capability and memory capacity. The server exhibits poor single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests (bottom 10%) and weak multi-core CPU performance (bottom 25%). Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached read/write operations consistently rank in the middle 50% tier. Passmark memory and database operations scores also achieve average ratings, indicating stable memory subsystem performance despite the constrained compute throughput.

Given the high memory density relative to the 8 vCPUs, this server is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. Appropriate workloads include medium-sized databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications. The qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, allowing users to host large datasets in memory without paying for unnecessary compute cores, though the lower CPU performance limits its utility for compute-heavy tasks like large-scale LLM inference.
